title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-22
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for debugging a throughput regression observed on Dedicated clusters after the recent continuous-batching config change. Mostly breadcrumbs, commands I ran, log snippets, quick hypotheses and next steps.

Summary of problem:
- Around 2025-11-17 we rolled out continuous-batching v2 config (auto-bucket + adaptive-threshold) to a subset of Dedicated capacity pools (pool-us-west-2-a).
- After rollout, several customers reported 20-40% QPS drop and 10-30% higher 99p latency on long-tail requests (seq len > 512).
- Not reproducible in staging with synthetic traffic; appears correlated with production sequence-length distribution and specific model variants (llama-2-13b-quant).

What I checked quickly (timeline):
- 11/18 09:12 - checked metrics dashboard (per-pool token/s and tail latency). Confirmed QPS drop aligning with rollout window.
- 11/18 09:30 - grabbed host-level telemetry from pool-us-west-2-a (nvidia-smi, dmesg). No OOMs, GPU util at ~60% (was 85% pre-rollout).
- 11/18 10:02 - rolled back continuous-batching feature gate on one canary host (host-37) - observed immediate return to prior throughput on that host within ~2min.
- 11/18 10:45 - reenabled batch size logging and tracer on runtime for more detail.

Commands and outputs (important ones):
- Check config on host:
  $ ssh host-37 
  $ cat /etc/redwood/runtime-config/continuous-batching.yaml
  batch_enabled: true
  adaptive_threshold_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  prefix_cache_enabled: true

- Metrics curl to local debug endpoint (host-37):
  $ curl -s http://localhost:6060/debug/batching | jq .
  {
    "current_batches": 48,
    "avg_batch_size": 3.2,
    "avg_wait_ms": 21.6,
    "batches_dropped": 0
  }
  Note: avg_batch_size=3.2 is much lower than expected (we typically see 6-8 for this pool).

- Runtime logs (snip) around the regression window:
  [2025-11-17T22:03:11Z] INFO serving.runtime.batch_queue: enqueued request request_id=... seq_len=764
  [2025-11-17T22:03:11Z] DEBUG serving.runtime.scheduling: bucket_assign: bucket_id=7 threshold_ms=12 current_wait=18
  [2025-11-17T22:03:11Z] WARN serving.runtime.kernel: kernel_choice=fast_attention fallback_to=naive_attention reason=kv_cache_mismatch
  [2025-11-17T22:03:12Z] INFO serving.runtime.batch_exec: executed batch_id=7 size=2 tokens_out=384 latency_ms=142

- Kernel fallback messages appear more frequently post-rollout. Example error: "kv_cache_mismatch: request cache index 128 != model kv length 0" - implies some cache keying or model state mismatch on quantized model path.

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Adaptive threshold too low for long-tail seqs: The v2 adaptive threshold (12ms) causes batches to flush early for large-seq requests, producing many small batches and lower GPU utilization. Evidence: avg_wait_ms=21.6 but avg_batch_size small; rollback on host fixed throughput.
2) Kernel selection regression for quantized variants: observed `fallback_to=naive_attention` and kv_cache_mismatch. Maybe continuous-batching interacts with KV cache positioning causing kernel selection to favor slower kernels for quantized weights.
3) Prefix cache interactions: prefix_cache_enabled=true - maybe range lookup latency for cached prefixes increases wait time or causes per-request overhead.
4) Scheduling/routing bug under adaptive buckets: bucket assignment code might be splitting requests across buckets incorrectly, reducing effective batching for sequences >512.

Quick experiments attempted and results:
- Disabled adaptive_threshold and set to fixed 32ms on host-37:
  result: avg_batch_size increased to ~6.5 and QPS returned to ~90% of pre-rollout baseline in 7m observation window. Supports hypothesis #1.
- Forced kernel hint to "preferred=fast_attention" in runtime flags for one replica:
  result: no measurable improvement; kernel logs still show occasional fallback. Indicates KB mismatch/incompatibility, not just hinting.
- Toggled prefix_cache_enabled=false:
  result: minor improvement (~5% throughput). Suggests prefix cache overhead is non-zero but not primary cause.

Unresolved error snippets to escalate to infra/research:
- Repro repro: kv_cache_mismatch only on quantized 13B variants and only when request payload includes system+user prompt with long static prefix (>1024 tokens historically). Need to capture deterministic repro.
- Stack trace for kernel fallback (excerpt):
  runtime/kernel_selector.cc:87  select_kernel_for_request()
  runtime/kv_cache_manager.cc:214 validate_or_clear_cache() 
  WARN: kv cache length mismatch, clearing cache for model=llama-2-13b-quant instance=inst-42

Notes on telemetry we should collect next:
- Per-request sequence length histogram with bucket boundaries at [64,128,256,512,1024,2048] for the affected pools (minute resolution) - to confirm distribution shift.
- Per-batch token count distribution and wait_ms distribution per bucket.
- Kernel fallback counts broken down by model variant and quantization type.
- Prefix cache hit/miss latency histogram.

Next steps / action items (me / others):
- [Asha] run a controlled canary in pool-us-west-2-a with adaptive_threshold=32ms and max_batch_tokens=16384 for 2 hours, collect metrics and logs (target: 1h of warm traffic). (in progress)
- [SRE - Jordan] capture host-level perf counters (L2/L3 caches, PCIe counters) for replica set during canary window.
- [ML infra - Gabriel] check kernel selection tests against quantized model suite; reproduce kv_cache_mismatch in a sandbox.
- [Release - Priya] hold further rollout of continuous-batching v2 until we confirm long-tail seqs behavior.

Open questions / things I want answered in follow-up:
- Was there any change to the quantization / model sharding path that coincided with the continuous-batching rollout? Link to model ingest commit?
- Do customers hitting the regression have a higher fraction of long static prefixes (system prompts) compared to baseline?
- Is the observed kernel fallback a conservative safety check (clearing cache) or symptomatic of real corruption?

Quick checklist for the canary (so I remember):
- [x] enable batch logging (batch size + wait_ms)
- [x] enable kernel fallback counters
- [x] capture per-request seq_len histogram
- [ ] run canary 2hrs (adaptive_threshold=32ms)
- [ ] collect traces for 5 slow requests (>99p) and attach request ids to ticket INF-2345

Linked artifacts / references:
- Jira: INF-2345 (throughput regression: continuous-batching v2 rollout)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/678 (continuous-batching v2 changes)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01XXXXXX/p169... (prod rollouts)

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- Could try a hybrid threshold that is sequence-length aware (larger windows for seq_len>512).
- Consider model-aware batching policy: prefer not to batch quantized 13B long-seq requests with short-chat requests.
- Add a metric: effective_tokens_per_gpu_second per model variant to expose per-model efficiency.

-- end of scratchpad --
